The first stable release of Nathéo came out on October 7, 2025, after two betas.

## Two betas before 1.0

1.0.0-beta.1, published in June 2025, was the first public release. It already covered the core of a CMS: pages and their preview, menus, FAQs, tags, comments and the media library. The administration managed users, site options, translations, logs and emails, and offered an SQL manager. The API v1, protected by tokens, served pages, menus, comments and options.

Beta 2, in September, added the first public site, with the Natheo-Horizon theme. It displayed the header and footer, menus, the breadcrumb, page content and comments, and generated the sitemap.

## What 1.0 added

The stable release mostly changed the tooling. The front end moved from Webpack Encore to Vite, the code was formatted with Prettier, and Symfony was updated to 7.3. Two bugs were also fixed, in the editor window when a page held several editors and in sending a test email.

A year later, 2.0 rebuilt the administration from the ground up.

name: content/page/blog/blog-2-0/1.en.md
before:
Nathéo 2.0 came out on November 7, 2026. This release reworks the administration screen by screen and changes the database schema.

## A new administration

Bootstrap was replaced by Tailwind CSS 4. Every screen was redone, from the login page to the page editor, with a dark mode and several color themes. The Vue 3 components are written in TypeScript, and the dashboard shows statistics and blocks that each user can configure.

The interface is translated into English and Spanish. Tests check that every label exists in the three languages.

## PostgreSQL

Nathéo now runs on PostgreSQL, in addition to MySQL and MariaDB. Schema updates go through Doctrine migrations, written for each of the two families. The post [One database, two platforms](/en/page/one-database-two-platforms) explains how.

## A security audit

Before the release, every module was audited: content, system, tools, API and public site. The administration grids escape entered values, actions sent in the background check a CSRF token, and permissions are checked for each piece of content. The fixed vulnerabilities are described in two security advisories published on GitHub.

## Before upgrading

The database schema changed too much for a 1.0 installation to be upgraded automatically. You need a fresh 2.0 installation, then to bring your content over. Version 2.0 requires PHP 8.4, and at least MySQL 8.2, MariaDB 10.11 or PostgreSQL 15.2.

[Download 2.0](https://github.com/counteraccro/natheo/releases/tag/v2.0.0)

name: content/page/blog/blog-2-1/1.en.md
before:
Nathéo 2.1 is out. After a 2.0 devoted to the administration, this release deals with page publishing and the public site.

## Drafts and validation

When you edit a page that is already live, your changes go into a draft. The published version stays on the site, and you can preview the draft on the site before publishing it. With the "Page validation" option, a contributor submits their page to an administrator, who finds it in the "Pages to review" block of the dashboard and approves it or rejects it with a reason.

## The API v2

The API was rewritten with API Platform and answers under `/api/v2`, in JSON-LD with Hydra or in plain JSON. It is documented with OpenAPI on `/api/v2/docs`. A user can open a session through the API, with a 15-minute access token and a refresh token to renew it. The API v1 remains available until 3.0, but no longer gets new features.

## The public site and its themes

The public site was rewritten to read all its data from the API v2. Themes rely on a shared base and are chosen in the system options. There are three of them: Natheo-Base, without styling, to start your own, the new version of Natheo-Horizon, which you are reading right now, and StormFront.

## In the administration

Image carousels arrive as a new content type, to place in a page block. The text editor becomes visual while still saving Markdown, and can have a text reviewed by an AI if you configure a provider. The media library gains search, multiple file selection and storage on an external server.

The details are in the [changelog](https://github.com/counteraccro/natheo/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md), and what comes next on the [roadmap](/en/page/roadmap).

before:
## Migrations written twice

Doctrine describes the entities once, but the SQL generated for migrations depends on the database. The same table is created with `INT AUTO_INCREMENT` on MySQL and with `GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY` on PostgreSQL, and indexes are declared inside the create statement on one side and separately on the other.

Each Nathéo migration therefore exists twice, with the same version number. They are stored by minor version of Nathéo, for example in `migrations/V2.1/Mysql` and `migrations/V2.1/Postgresql`. When migrations run, a dedicated class looks at the platform of the connection and loads only the matching folders. A second class sorts the migrations by their number, which holds the date, whatever folder they are in.

Each file also starts with a platform check. A MySQL migration run by mistake on PostgreSQL is skipped instead of failing halfway.

## Portable SQL

Hand-written data updates raise another problem. Some syntax exists on a single platform: `UPDATE … JOIN` and `REGEXP` on MySQL, `UPDATE … FROM` and the `~` operator on PostgreSQL. In that case, the query is written twice, once in each file.

Reserved words need care too. The users table is called `user`, a reserved word. It is wrapped in backticks in the Doctrine mapping, which Doctrine turns into double quotes on PostgreSQL. In hand-written SQL, the name is protected with `quoteSingleIdentifier()`, which picks the right characters for the connected database.

Tests check all of this. On every pull request, GitHub Actions runs the whole PHPUnit suite twice, on MySQL 8.4 and on PostgreSQL 16, and both must pass before the merge.

## Getting a token

A call to the API v2 requires a token. Create it in the administration, from the "API tokens" menu of the "System" section, with the role that matches your use: read, write or admin. The token is sent in the `Authorization: Bearer` header. The "Open the API?" option must be on.

## Finding a page

A page is looked up by its address, with the `slug` filter on the pages collection. The language is chosen with the `Accept-Language` header or the `locale` parameter.

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
     -H "Accept-Language: en" \
     "https://your-site.com/api/v2/pages?slug=home"
```

The response is a Hydra collection holding 0 or 1 page. Each page appears with a summary: its identifier, title, author, tags and dates.

## Reading the page and its blocks

A call to `/api/v2/pages/{id}` returns the full page, with its layout, SEO information, menus and the list of its blocks. Each block is referred to by its IRI, for example `/api/v2/page_contents/476`. That call returns the content of the block, with the Markdown already converted to HTML for a text block.

For JSON without the Hydra fields, add the `Accept: application/json` header.

The full list of resources, their parameters and their errors is on `/api/v2/docs`, where each call can be tried with your token. If you still use the API v1, the [migration guide](https://counteraccro.github.io/natheo.doc/Docs/API/migration_v2.html) describes the changes.

## System options

Site settings are made in the administration, from the "System options" menu of the "System" section. Options are sorted into categories.

- Website: the name and address of the site, the default language, the public site theme, whether it is open to the public, and the footer content, with links to social networks.
- SEO: options that ask search engines not to index the site or not to follow its links.
- Administration: page validation, confirmation before leaving a form, the number of rows in tables and permission to delete data.
- API: whether the API is open and how long user sessions last.
- Comments: whether comments are open and whether new comments must be approved.

The Media library, Emails, Notifications and Logs categories set where files are stored, the sender of emails, the purge of notifications and the history of database changes.

As long as the "Open the site to the public?" option is off, visitors see a holding page instead of the site.

## The database

The `.env` configuration targets MariaDB. For PostgreSQL, change `DATABASE_URL` and enable the `pdo_pgsql` extension. Nathéo detects the platform and loads the migrations that match it. The [database page](https://counteraccro.github.io/natheo.doc/Docs/Demarrage/base_de_donnees.html) of the documentation gives the details.

## Background tasks

Sending emails and exporting the database from the "Database" tool go through a Messenger queue. For these tasks to be processed, a process must run continuously.

```bash
php bin/console messenger:consume async
```

In production, run it with a process manager such as Supervisor, and set `MAILER_DSN` in `.env.local` to send emails.

## Overriding the API and the administration

The API and the administration screens can be customised without changing Nathéo's code. Your code goes in `src/Overwrite/` for PHP and in `assets/overwrite/` for screens.

### An API operation

Each API operation has a name, shown in the API documentation (`info_get`, `admin_tag_patch`…). In `config/cms/overwrite.yaml`, an entry gives an operation another provider for a read, or another processor for a write. The operation keeps its address and its rights.

```yaml
overwrite:
    api:
        - operation: info_get
          provider: App\Overwrite\Api\State\Provider\System\InfoProvider
```

The replacement class receives the original provider in its constructor, calls it, then completes its response. The file is read when the cache is built. After a change in production, run `php bin/console cache:clear`, which rejects an unknown operation or a class that does not exist.

### An administration screen

A file placed in `assets/overwrite/vue/Components/Admin/` replaces the file with the same path in `assets/vue/Components/Admin/`. For example, `assets/overwrite/vue/Components/Admin/Ui/Form/UiButton.vue` replaces the button of the whole back-office. A new screen is declared in a `module.ts` in `assets/overwrite/vue/Components/Admin/Modules/<Module>/`, and its module class, which sets the required role and the menu entry, in `src/Overwrite/Module/`. Run `yarn build` again after each addition.

### The bundled example

Nathéo ships with an example. The provider of `GET /api/v2/info` is overridden to fill the `extra` field. The "Override example" screen of the "Tools" section, open to the super administrator, shows this response and goes through each step of this page as a tutorial, with the code of the example files. To remove it, delete its entry from `config/cms/overwrite.yaml` and the files listed on its screen.

## Las opciones del sistema

Los ajustes del sitio se hacen en la administración, desde el menú «Opciones del sistema» de la parte «Sistema». Las opciones están ordenadas por categorías.

- Sitio web: el nombre y la dirección del sitio, el idioma por defecto, el tema del sitio público, su apertura al público y el contenido del pie de página, con los enlaces a las redes sociales.
- SEO: las opciones que piden a los buscadores que no indexen el sitio o que no sigan sus enlaces.
- Administración: la validación de páginas, la confirmación antes de salir de un formulario, el número de filas de las tablas y el permiso para eliminar datos.
- API: la apertura de la API y la duración de las sesiones de los usuarios.
- Comentarios: la apertura de los comentarios y la validación obligatoria de los nuevos comentarios.

Las categorías Mediateca, Correos electrónicos, Notificaciones y Logs configuran dónde se guardan los archivos, el remitente de los correos, la purga de las notificaciones y el historial de cambios en la base.

Mientras la opción «¿Abrir el sitio al público?» esté desactivada, los visitantes ven una página de espera en lugar del sitio.

## La base de datos

La configuración de `.env` apunta a MariaDB. Para PostgreSQL, cambie `DATABASE_URL` y active la extensión `pdo_pgsql`. Nathéo detecta la plataforma y carga las migraciones que le corresponden. La [página sobre la base de datos](https://counteraccro.github.io/natheo.doc/Docs/Demarrage/base_de_donnees.html) de la documentación da los detalles.

## Las tareas en segundo plano

El envío de los correos y la exportación de la base desde la herramienta «Base de datos» pasan por una cola Messenger. Para que estas tareas se procesen, un proceso debe ejecutarse de forma continua.

```bash
php bin/console messenger:consume async
```

En producción, láncelo con un gestor de procesos como Supervisor, e indique `MAILER_DSN` en `.env.local` para el envío de los correos.

## Sobrescribir la API y la administración

La API y las pantallas de la administración se personalizan sin modificar el código de Nathéo. Su código va en `src/Overwrite/` para el PHP y en `assets/overwrite/` para las pantallas.

### Una operación de la API

Cada operación de la API lleva un nombre, visible en la documentación de la API (`info_get`, `admin_tag_patch`…). En `config/cms/overwrite.yaml`, una entrada da a una operación otro provider para una lectura, u otro processor para una escritura. La operación conserva su dirección y sus permisos.

```yaml
overwrite:
    api:
        - operation: info_get
          provider: App\Overwrite\Api\State\Provider\System\InfoProvider
```

La clase de sustitución recibe el provider original en su constructor, lo llama y luego completa su respuesta. El archivo se lee al construir la caché. Tras una modificación en producción, ejecute `php bin/console cache:clear`, que rechaza una operación desconocida o una clase que no existe.

### Una pantalla de la administración

Un archivo colocado en `assets/overwrite/vue/Components/Admin/` sustituye al archivo con la misma ruta en `assets/vue/Components/Admin/`. Por ejemplo, `assets/overwrite/vue/Components/Admin/Ui/Form/UiButton.vue` sustituye al botón de todo el back-office. Una pantalla nueva se declara en un `module.ts` de `assets/overwrite/vue/Components/Admin/Modules/<Module>/`, y su clase de módulo, que fija el rol necesario y la entrada del menú, en `src/Overwrite/Module/`. Vuelva a ejecutar `yarn build` tras cada añadido.

### El ejemplo incluido

Nathéo incluye un ejemplo. El provider de `GET /api/v2/info` se sobrescribe para rellenar el campo `extra`. La pantalla «Ejemplo de sobrescritura» de la sección «Herramientas», reservada al superadministrador, muestra esta respuesta y retoma cada paso de esta página en forma de tutorial, con el código de los archivos del ejemplo. Para quitarlo, elimine su entrada de `config/cms/overwrite.yaml` y los archivos indicados en su pantalla.

## The base and the themes

All public site themes rely on a shared base. It holds the TypeScript types of the API v2 resources, a client that handles authentication, pagination and errors, and Vue composables such as `usePage`, `usePageBlocks`, `useMenus` or `useComments`. A theme never calls the API directly. Its components get the data through these composables and take care of displaying it.

## The architecture

The base is shared by all themes. Each theme adds its own files, here for a `my_theme` theme.

```text
assets/
├── ts/Front/Api/                       resource types (base)
├── vue/Composables/Front/              API client and composables (base)
├── front_my_theme.ts                   Vite entry of the theme
├── styles/app_front_my_theme.css       theme styles
├── vue/controllers/Front/MyTheme/
│   └── App.vue                         root component
└── vue/Components/Front/MyTheme/       header, blocks, menus, comments…
templates/front/my_theme/
├── index.html.twig                     mounts Front/MyTheme/App
└── close.html.twig                     page shown when the site is closed
```

## Declaring the theme

The theme is added to the `App\Enum\Front\Template` enum and to the list of the `OS_THEME_FRONT_SITE` option, in `config/cms/options_system.yaml`.

```php
case MY_THEME = 'my_theme';
```

```yaml
list_value: 'natheo_horizon:Natheo-Horizon|natheo_base:Natheo-Base|my_theme:My theme'
```

Its Vite entry, declared in `vite.config.mts` under the name `front_my_theme`, loads its styles and its components.

```ts
import './styles/app_front_my_theme.css';
import { startVueControllers } from './bootstrap';

startVueControllers(import.meta.glob('./vue/controllers/Front/MyTheme/**/*.vue'));
```

## Writing the components

The root component receives the props prepared by the server and creates the site context with `createFrontContext()`. The other composables then find it on their own.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { createFrontContext } from '@/vue/Composables/Front/useFrontContext';
import { usePage } from '@/vue/Composables/Front/usePage';
import type { FrontThemeProps } from '@/ts/Front/FrontProps.type';

const props = defineProps<FrontThemeProps>();
createFrontContext(props);
const { data: page, loading } = usePage();
</script>
```

For blocks, `usePageBlocks` receives one component per block type and returns the list of the page blocks, each with its width (`full`, `half` or `third`). The theme picks the classes that match these widths.

```ts
const { blocks } = usePageBlocks(page, { text: BlockText, faq: BlockFaq, listing: BlockListing });
```

`useMenus(page)` works the same way for menus. It sorts them by position, and `layoutOf(menu)` gives their display type (`dropdown`, `mega`, `sidebar`, `accordion`…).

The easiest way is to start from a copy of Natheo-Base, which displays every layout, every block type and every menu in semantic HTML, without any styling. The theme then appears in the "Theme of your site" option.

Un thème n'appelle jamais l'API directement. Ses composants récupèrent les données par ces composables et s'occupent de les afficher.

## L'architecture

Le socle est partagé par tous les thèmes. Chaque thème ajoute ses propres fichiers, ici pour un thème `my_theme`.

```text
assets/
├── ts/Front/Api/                       types des ressources (socle)
├── vue/Composables/Front/              client de l'API et composables (socle)
├── front_my_theme.ts                   entrée Vite du thème
├── styles/app_front_my_theme.css       styles du thème
├── vue/controllers/Front/MyTheme/
│   └── App.vue                         composant racine
└── vue/Components/Front/MyTheme/       en-tête, blocs, menus, commentaires…
templates/front/my_theme/
├── index.html.twig                     monte Front/MyTheme/App
└── close.html.twig                     page affichée quand le site est fermé
```

Le thème s'ajoute à l'enum `App\Enum\Front\Template` et à la liste de l'option `OS_THEME_FRONT_SITE`, dans `config/cms/options_system.yaml`.

```php
case MY_THEME = 'my_theme';
```

```yaml
list_value: 'natheo_horizon:Natheo-Horizon|natheo_base:Natheo-Base|my_theme:Mon thème'
```

Son entrée Vite, déclarée dans `vite.config.mts` sous le nom `front_my_theme`, charge ses styles et ses composants.

```ts
import './styles/app_front_my_theme.css';
import { startVueControllers } from './bootstrap';

startVueControllers(import.meta.glob('./vue/controllers/Front/MyTheme/**/*.vue'));
```

Le composant racine reçoit les props préparées par le serveur et crée le contexte du site avec `createFrontContext()`. Les autres composables le retrouvent ensuite tout seuls.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { createFrontContext } from '@/vue/Composables/Front/useFrontContext';
import { usePage } from '@/vue/Composables/Front/usePage';
import type { FrontThemeProps } from '@/ts/Front/FrontProps.type';

const props = defineProps<FrontThemeProps>();
createFrontContext(props);
const { data: page, loading } = usePage();
</script>
```

Pour les blocs, `usePageBlocks` reçoit un composant par type de bloc et renvoie la liste des blocs de la page, chacun avec sa largeur (`full`, `half` ou `third`). Le thème choisit les classes qui correspondent à ces largeurs.

```ts
const { blocks } = usePageBlocks(page, { text: BlockText, faq: BlockFaq, listing: BlockListing });
```

`useMenus(page)` fonctionne de la même façon pour les menus. Il les range par position, et `layoutOf(menu)` donne leur type d'affichage (`dropdown`, `mega`, `sidebar`, `accordion`…).

Le plus simple est de partir d'une copie de Natheo-Base, qui affiche toutes les dispositions, tous les types de blocs et tous les menus en HTML sémantique, sans aucun style. Le thème apparaît ensuite dans l'option « Thème de votre site ».

## Hydra resources

The API v2 is built with API Platform and served under `/api/v2`. It exposes pages and their blocks, menus, comments, the public site options and the sitemap, along with the account and sessions of the logged-in user.

Responses use JSON-LD with the Hydra vocabulary. A resource linked to another one refers to it by its IRI, for example `/api/v2/pages/12`, and includes a summary of its useful fields. Collections are paginated by 20 items, up to 100 on request with `itemsPerPage`. A client that prefers plain JSON gets it with the `Accept: application/json` header.

Lookups go through exact filters on collections. A page is found from its address with `GET /api/v2/pages?slug=api-v2`, and the menus of a position with the `position` filter.

## Authentication

The API v2 offers two ways to authenticate.

The first one uses an API token. It is created in the administration, from the "API tokens" menu, with a read, write or admin role. This is what you use to connect an external application or an import script to Nathéo. The public site works the same way, with a token created during installation.

A user can list their open sessions through the API and close each one separately.

In both cases, the token is sent in the `Authorization: Bearer` header. The "Open the API?" system option cuts off all access at once.
